newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ALPHA INVEST SAYS 96 NET UP 7.2PCT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ALPHA INVEST SAYS 96 NET UP 7.2PCT.

text.p: Greek closed-end fund Alpha Invest posted net profit of 4.58 billion drachmas in 1996, up 7.2 percent on 1995, and will pay a net dividend per share of 375 drachmas, up 13 percent, its chairman said.
"The performance of the company was satisfactory despite the lukewarm climate in the domestic market," Constantine Kyriakopoulos told the annual shareholders meeting.
Alpha Invest is a subsidiary of Alpha Credit Bank.

"The dividend of 375 drachmas per share appears to be the same as in the previous fiscal year. But, in reality, it is higher by 13.4 percent because it is paid net after the change in the tax status of investment companies," he said.
The dividend will be payable on April 23.
